pdmS7 is a probability-distributed rainfall-runoff model (Moore, 2007) built for one purpose: to
calibrate conceptual models fairly, record that calibration so it can be defended, and compare
the result with machine-learning models on equal terms. Different readers need different parts.
Pick the role closest to yours and read the articles in order. The [Glossary](glossary.html)
explains any term along the way.

# I calibrate models (Custodian)

1. [How the PDM works](pdm-explained.html): what the model does, in plain English.
2. [Preparing your data](data-preparation.html): from EA sources to model files, with a
   checklist.
3. [Your first model run](example-workflow.html): data to a calibrated, saved model.
4. [Starting a run](starting-states.html) and [Choosing model components](model-options.html).
5. [Scoring a simulation](scoring.html): what each score shows.
6. [Automatic calibration, explained](auto-calibration.html), including staged calibration.
7. [Logging a manual calibration](calibration-log.html): the record a Steward will review.
8. [Choosing a model structure](choosing-structure.html), when the standard PDM may not suit.

For many catchments at once, add [Calibrating many catchments](many-catchments.html).
[Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.html) covers the common errors.

# I review and sign off calibrations (Steward)

1. [Reviewing a calibration: a Steward's guide](steward-guide.html): what to look at and what
   should make you stop.
2. [Scoring a simulation](scoring.html): enough to read the report's scores.
3. [Logging a manual calibration](calibration-log.html): how the record is built.
4. [Inside the logs](log-structure.html): what the checksums prove.

# I am accountable for a model's use (Owner)

1. This page and the [Steward's guide](steward-guide.html), for what sign-off means.
2. [The benchmark protocol](../benchmark-protocol.html), if the model is part of the comparison
   with machine learning.
3. [Calibration log design](../calibration-log-design.html), for the governance decisions behind
   the log.

# I forecast

1. [How the PDM works](pdm-explained.html).
2. [Forecast updating](forecast-updating.html): state correction and error prediction.
3. [AR and ARMA error correction, explained](ar-error-correction.html): what the IMFS
   coefficients mean.
4. [Testing forecasts with hindcasts](hindcasts.html): skill by lead time against persistence.
5. [Scoring a simulation](scoring.html), for the threshold scores POD, FAR and CSI.

# I build the LSTM side of the comparison

1. [The benchmark protocol](../benchmark-protocol.html): data, periods, effort and scoring,
   fixed in advance.
2. [Scoring a simulation](scoring.html): the scoring function both models are judged by.
3. [Testing forecasts with hindcasts](hindcasts.html): how forecasts from any model are scored.
4. [How the PDM works](pdm-explained.html), to know what the LSTM is up against.

# I develop or maintain the package

1. [Model equations](model-equations.html): every equation, with Moore's numbering.
2. [The C core](compiled-core.html): speed, equivalence tests and use from other languages.
3. The Guides menu: validation, source notes, benchmark timing and the roadmap.
4. [Further reading](further-reading.html).
